messages:
Sophia: Windows Defender quarantined redwoodctl installer, had to restore & allow. After that redwoodctl runs but 'redwoodctl profile merge' during first-run throws PermissionError when touching %APPDATA%\redwood\profiles.json. redwoodctl login keeps opening browser then error 503, and localserve sample app shows 'stale token' even after login. Anyone seen this? (Windows 10, Defender Ent. build 19045)

mike_devex: ugh. Do you remember the exact path Defender quarantined? sometimes it blocks the signed exe on corporate endpoints.

Sophia: path was C:\Users\sophia\Downloads\redwoodctl-windows-x64.exe, Defender quarantined it then restored. I ran as admin to copy to C:\Program Files\Redwood\bin.

kevin_infra: Defender can leave the file blocked via alternate data stream / zone.identifier. Try: right-click -> Properties -> Unblock. Or run: 
```
Get-Item 'C:\Program Files\Redwood\bin\redwoodctl.exe' | Unblock-File
```

Sophia: tried Unblock-File, still seeing profile merge error. stacktrace:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "redwoodctl\config.py", line 132, in merge_profiles
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: 'C:\Users\sophia\AppData\Roaming\redwood\profiles.json'
```

carla: could be that installer created files under SYSTEM account then user can't overwrite. Did you install 'for all users'? Check file owner.

Sophia: oh I ran installer with admin and selected 'Install for all users'. File owner is SYSTEM indeed.

mike_devex: yeah that's the issue. Quick fix: change ownership to your user and set ACLs:
```
takeown /F "C:\Users\sophia\AppData\Roaming\redwood\profiles.json"
icacls "C:\Users\sophia\AppData\Roaming\redwood" /grant %USERNAME%:F /t
```

Sophia: thanks, ownership fix allowed profile write.

Sophia: but login still weird: redwoodctl login opens browser to device code, I paste code, it spins then browser returns 503. CLI logs show 'auth: upstream 503: service overloaded'.

kevin_infra: that's a separate issue — could be guardian proxy at corp network returning 503 for redirect. Try `redwoodctl login --headless` to use device code flow entirely in terminal.

Sophia: ran `redwoodctl login --headless` and it worked, token saved. localserve sample app still shows stale token error when hitting /api/generate.

carla: localserve uses REDWOOD_PROFILE env var sometimes. `redwoodctl profile list` to confirm active profile and `redwoodctl profile get default` to inspect token expiry.

Sophia: `redwoodctl profile list` shows two entries: default and default-1. maybe merge created duplicate. localserve was reading default-1.

mike_devex: localserve picks up profile via config at %APPDATA%/redwood/localserve.json or env REDWOOD_PROFILE. Maybe the installer left localserve config referencing old profile id. Inspect and fix or run `redwoodctl localserve --reinit-config`.

Sophia: ran `redwoodctl localserve --reinit-config`, restarted app, now works. Summary for docs:
- Defender quarantine can leave zone.identifier => Unblock-File
- Installer 'Install for all users' may set SYSTEM ownership on profiles.json
- Use takeown/icacls to fix ownership
- If browser login fails on corp network, use `--headless`
- localserve may reference stale profile; `--reinit-config` resets to current profile

mike_devex: can you paste minimal repro + steps into the devex handbook? we'll add a troubleshooting checklist. :thumbsup:

Sophia: will do, adding paths and commands

infra-bot: new doc created: /handbook/devex/windows-ctl-installer-troubleshoot (created by sophia)

mike_devex: thanks!
